title: Rate limits & org/project keys demo with Seabreeze Health
summary: Redwood walked through org/project keys, rate limiting policies, quotas, and console controls. Customer is interested in per-team project keys, burst behavior, and private/VPC deployment options. Security team requested SOC2 + KMS details and a pilot with a benchmark. Next steps: pricing, SOC2 docs, pilot plan and sample traffic.
topics: Per-project / per-route rate limits and quotas
Console demos: dashboards, billing, token-level cost
Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization
next_steps: Alicia to send pricing + pilot scope by 2026-11-16
Marco to share benchmark plan and run initial perf test with Seabreeze sample traffic by 2026-11-20
Seabreeze to provide SSO SAML metadata and team traffic patterns by 2026-11-15
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting (30m) after docs are shared
action_items: Alicia Chen - Send pricing deck, pilot scope, and example contract language - due 2026-11-16
Marco Diaz - Draft benchmark/test plan and share test harness + expected metrics - due 2026-11-20
Sara Nguyen - Provide SSO/SAML metadata and per-team traffic profiles - due 2026-11-15
Mike Harper - Confirm retention and KMS questions for SOC 2 review - due 2026-11-18
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alicia from Redwood Inference, i run the east accounts. quick intro, we have Marco here from our engineering team who will run through the demo.
[00:12] David (Seabreeze CTO): Hi all, david here, sara and mike are with me, thanks for doing this.
[00:18] Marco (Redwood SE): hey hi, thanks. we'll focus on org keys and rate-limits, and then show the console and an optimize walkthrough. feel free to jump in.
[00:30] Sara (Head of Platform): high level — we run a mix of on-prem and cloud, we have some models on sagemaker and some internal infra, our ask is per-team quotas and clear multi-tenant controls.
[00:42] Mike (Security): and from security we want to understand VPC/private deployment, key management, and audit trails — SOC 2 is a hard ask.
[00:50] Alicia: totally, we get that often. quick qualification, what's your target timeline for a pilot?
[00:56] David: hoping to start a pilot in the next 3-4 weeks, 2-3 internal teams, and then expand by Q1.
[01:05] Marco: sounds good. ok zooming into product — first concept is org vs project keys. we show a screenshot of the console — top-left you can see organization admin, under that projects for each team.
[01:20] Marco: Org keys are for org-wide billing and admin controls, project keys are meant to be embedded per-service/team. each project can have its own quotas and rate-limits.
[01:34] Leah (SRE): how are keys scoped? can we rotate per project and revoke without impacting others?
[01:38] Marco: yes, you can rotate and revoke at the project level, the console and api support key lifecycle. revoking a project key only affects that project, not the rest of the org.
[01:49] Alicia: i'll also call out that we support role-based access at the org/project level — read-only, billing, admin, etc.
[01:56] Sara: and billing granularity — can we get token-level cost per project?
[02:02] Marco: yes we have token-level breakdowns and per-route breakdowns in the billing dashboard. you can export CSVs or hook up to our usage API.
[02:10] David: good. show us how rate-limits are configured.
[02:15] Marco: demo — navigating to policies, you can create a policy attached to projects or routes. for example per-project QPS, per-route points, and quota windows. here's a sample: project: "clinical-nlp", limit: 200 rps, burst: 400, monthly quota: 5M tokens.
[02:34] Marco: note on burst — burst is handled by a token-bucket token concept, it's configurable and spikes route to backup variants if sustained. also fallback routing to cheaper model variants if you hit capacity.
[02:48] Mike: when you say fallback, does that surface to users? can we control which teams get fallback vs hard reject?
[02:55] Marco: yes you can set policy behavior per project — either soft-fallback to a compatible model variant, or hard reject with 429. so teams can choose strictness.
[03:06] Sara: any rate-limit enforcement at the edge vs at the runtime? we want low-latency checks.
[03:12] Marco: enforcement is at the smart routing layer near the edge; we try to keep checks local to reduce latency, and we maintain consistent counters across regional shards.
[03:21] David: performance — curious about overhead of these checks, does it add significant p99?
[03:27] Marco: typically microseconds-level in our tests, most overhead is in networking and model inference. we showed earlier benchmarks where rate-limits don't materially change p99. we can run a bench with your traffic.
[03:38] Alicia: quick note on quotas — admins can set monthly or yearly quotas and receive alerts as usage approaches thresholds.
[03:46] Marco: switching to the console demo now, here is the project list, clicking into "clinical-nlp" we see usage graphs, active keys, rate-limit policy attached, and billing breakdown. you can also create service tokens for backends with limited scopes.
[04:05] Marco: small transcription glitch — console image labeled "Redwood dedidcated" in our slide, that should be "Redwood Dedicated".
[04:12] David: haha ok noted.
[04:15] Marco: next is programmatic controls, our API supports passing an X-Project-Key header, or you can use org key with project_id in request. here's an example curl snippet...
[04:34] Marco: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <project_key>" \nPOST /v1/generate \n-d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"summarize"}'
[04:50] Leah: on telemetry — will we get per-request trace ids and the original project id in logs?
[04:55] Marco: yes all request logs include project id, route, model, and request id. audit logs are available via the console and can be shipped to your SIEM.
[05:06] Mike: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys? can we bring our own KMS / HSM?
[05:11] Alicia: yes we support integrations with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys in Private deployments; for hosted we offer managed keys but provide options for bring-your-own in Private or Dedicated setups.
[05:22] Marco: also note the Private deployment includes an optional on-prem package for air-gapped environments.
[05:29] David: good. tell us about quotas across multi-tenant teams — how do we allocate and move quota?
[05:35] Marco: admins can allocate quotas to projects, and transfer is manual through the console or via API. we also have an autoscale/burst credit pool for orgs that want shared burst capacity; that is helpful for occasional spikes.
[05:48] Sara: autoscale policies — can we set per-project burst budgets and priorities?
[05:53] Marco: yes you can set priority weights and reserved capacity for critical projects. non-critical traffic can be deprioritized during constrained conditions.
[06:04] David: what's the billing unit — tokens or calls?
[06:08] Marco: tokens; we bill per-token for generation and per-embedding for embeddings, but you can map charges to projects for internal chargeback.
[06:16] Alicia: example: monthly billing CSV shows project id, tokens, cost, and cost per route.
[06:23] Leah: any special compliance features for healthcare — data residency, retention policies?
[06:29] Mike: yes also need audit trail retention for 7 years for some records.
[06:34] Marco: we offer configurable retention windows and can integrate with your log retention policies in Private. for hosted, longer retention and custom retention are available as an add-on. we can include retention SLAs in enterprise contract.
[06:47] Sara: let's get into Optimize briefly — can the product suggest batching and quantization profiles per workload?
[06:53] Marco: yes Optimize will analyze call patterns and recommend batching sizes, cache policies, and quantization model suggestions to reduce cost while keeping quality. it'll surface expected token savings.
[07:06] David: showcasing a real example would help — do you have a past case of 30% token saving?
[07:11] Marco: we do, in one case with high prefix reuse and caching we saw 25-35% savings; we'll share an anonymized benchmark.
[07:20] Alicia: are there licensing or commitment requirements for Dedicated or Private?
[07:25] Marco: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; Private has licensing + support fees. for pilots we often do a time-boxed pilot on hosted with a path to Dedicated.
[07:36] Mike: security question — SSO/SAML and RBAC, do you support SCIM provisioning?
[07:41] Marco: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user groups and RBAC are supported.
[07:46] Leah: how do we test performance for our traffic shape? can you simulate thousands of concurrent calls?
[07:52] Marco: yes, we'll run a bench using your sample traffic pattern; we have a test harness that can replay traces. Alicia will coordinate access and sample data.
[08:01] Alicia: i'll pick this up in next steps.
[08:05] Marco: back to rate-limits, small note on eventual consistency — counters are strongly consistent within a region for most policies, cross-region counters may have small windows; we document exact behavior.
[08:18] David: any retry behavior you recommend?
[08:21] Marco: exponential backoff for 429s, and prefer idempotent retries; for hard-reject policies it's better to surface an error.
[08:30] Sara: show us the policy UI for rules chaining — e.g. rule A applies to route X unless project Y has override.
[08:37] Marco: demo — policy precedence: project overrides org, route-level overrides project for that route; we can add exception lists by project id.
[08:48] Mike: about logs — do we get full payloads or redacted content in logs?
[08:53] Marco: by default payloads are redacted for PII in hosted, and in Private you control logging. we support field-level redaction rules.
[09:03] David: ok practical ask — we want a 2-week pilot, 3 teams, 2M tokens per month total, with one team requiring private network. can you support that?
[09:12] Alicia: yes, pilot model: hosted with VPC peering for the one team, create projects and keys, and a dedicated burst pool kept for you — we'll map billing to your org.
[09:21] Marco: we'll include a benchmark run and a runbook for onboarding.
[09:24] Sara: demo the alerting — how do we get notified as they near quota?
[09:29] Marco: alert rules can be set on percent thresholds; we can notify via email, webhooks, or your PagerDuty.
[09:36] Mike: vendor comparison — openai was simpler but we need better enterprise controls. how do you contrast?
[09:42] Alicia: we position as production-first, with unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and richer multi-tenant controls. we also give clear levers to control cost like Optimize.
[09:53] David: any pitfalls we should watch for?
[09:56] Marco: main pitfalls: underallocating burst for real spikes, not instrumenting prefix reuse for caching, and not using project keys leading to poor cost visibility.
[10:06] Alicia: pipeline for the next steps — i'll send pricing and pilot scope, Marco will send bench plan.
[10:12] Marco: quick note — some terms in our slides are abbreviated, e.g., "KV cache" got transcribed as "kay vee cache" in earlier auto notes, ignore that.
[10:20] Sara: cool, thanks.
[10:24] — TRANSCRIPT SNIPPET —
[12:15] Marco: (walks through UI) click policies -> new policy -> scope project -> set rate limit 200 rps -> set burst 400 -> set fallback behavior to "soft-fallback" -> save. it applies immediately.
[15:40] Leah: when you apply it does it roll out with a canary?
[15:44] Marco: you can canary by project or percentage rollout; we have rollout controls.
[18:30] David: are logs exportable to s3?
[18:34] Marco: yes export to S3 or push to your SIEM via HTTP sink.
[21:10] Mike: how about per-route quotas for embeddings vs generation?
[21:14] Marco: yes different quotas by route type; you can set tokens-per-route monthly quotas.
[24:00] Alicia: just flagging we will attach SOC2 and network diagram in the follow-up email.
[27:30] Sara: ok pricing model?
[27:35] Alicia: starter usage pricing for hosted plus a pilot discount, Dedicated has reserved rates based on commit. i'll include concrete numbers.
[30:00] Marco: one more demo detail — the Optimize tab runs a one-click analysis on a sample of your traffic, and recommendations are exportable.
[33:15] David: very helpful. any blockers to starting pilot?
[33:20] Sara: we need SAML metadata and confirmation of retention for audit.
[33:24] Mike: add KMS integration details.
[33:28] Alicia: noted.
[36:00] Marco: we'll run the bench using your sample traffic, expected to take 2-3 days for initial results.
[39:15] David: ok let's wrap.
[39:20] Alicia: recap: we'll send pricing, SOC2 docs, pilot scope and benchmark plan. seabeaze? seabreeze? (laughs) — Seabreeze to share SAML metadata and traffic patterns.
[39:35] Sara: i'll send those by monday the 15th.
[39:40] Marco: action items recap — see the follow-up email for assigned owners.
[39:45] David: thanks everyone.
[39:47] Alicia: thanks all, talk soon.
[44:30] call end
